title: 《Give and Take》— 好书精读 Read 84
title_en: Give and Take — Deep Reading Read 84

questions.question: 按《Give and Take》，同样是给予者，有人落在业绩榜底部、有人登顶，分水岭在哪里？
options: 是否在关心他人和关心自己之间各让一半、取个折中
给予的总量多少，给得越多越容易被榨干垫底
是否在关心他人的同时也同样精明地关心自己
是否只帮那些日后有能力回报自己的人
questions.explanation: 格兰特把关心他人与关心自己看成两条独立的轴：两条都拉满的「利他兼利己」者登顶，只剩前一条的「无私」者垫底。各让一半的折中恰恰是把两条轴误当成一根跷跷板。
questions.question_en: In Give and Take, some givers end up at the bottom of the performance ladder and others at the top. What separates them?
options_en: Whether they split the difference, giving up half of each kind of concern
How much they give: the more they give, the likelier they burn out at the bottom
Whether they look out for their own interests as shrewdly as they care about others
Whether they only help people who can repay them later
questions.explanation_en: Grant treats concern for others and concern for self as two independent axes. 'Otherish' givers score high on both and rise; selfless givers have only the first and sink. Splitting the difference mistakes the two axes for a single seesaw.

questions.question: 书中解释给予在长期里为什么会变成优势，靠的是什么结构性机制？
options: 管理层偏爱乐于助人的员工，会优先提拔他们
给予者在帮忙中积累了更多技能，最终凭个人能力胜出
人数最多的互利者会主动惩罚索取者、回报给予者，回报多来自旁观者
被帮过的人迟早会良心发现，把当初得到的好处加倍奉还给当初的给予者
questions.explanation: 格兰特明确说「善有善报」在心理学上站不住：给予者的回报很少来自被帮的那个人，而来自看在眼里的互利者，他们维护公平、惩罚索取者、回报给予者。
questions.question_en: What structural mechanism does the book offer for why giving pays off in the long run?
options_en: Managers favor helpful employees and promote them first
Givers build more skills while helping and ultimately win on individual ability
Matchers, the majority, punish takers and reward givers, so the payback comes from bystanders
People who were helped eventually feel grateful and repay the giver several times over
questions.explanation_en: Grant explicitly rejects 'good deeds get rewarded' as psychologically weak. The return rarely comes from the person helped; it comes from watching matchers, who enforce fairness by punishing takers and rewarding givers.

questions.question: 按书中的说法，识别「随和的索取者」（伪装者）最可靠的线索是什么？
options: 看行为是否不对称：对上对下是否两副面孔，讲成果说「我」还是「我们」
看态度是否始终热情客气，过分好相处、从不得罪人的人多半另有所图
看他在团队里的人缘，人缘越好越说明大家都欠过他人情
看他是否经常拒绝别人的请求，懂得拒绝的人通常也更会替自己打算盘
questions.explanation: 随和是外观，给予还是索取是动机，两者互相独立，所以看态度识别不了伪装者。格兰特给的办法是看行为的不对称：对上司和对前台是不是两副面孔、讲成果时用「我」还是「我们」。
questions.question_en: According to the book, what is the most reliable way to spot an agreeable taker (a 'faker')?
options_en: Look for asymmetry: different faces up and down the ladder, 'I' versus 'we' when describing results
Watch their manner: someone who is overly warm and pleasant usually has an agenda
Check their popularity: the better liked they are, the more people owe them favors
See whether they often turn down requests, since people who say no tend to look out for themselves
questions.explanation_en: Agreeableness is a surface style while giving versus taking is a motive, and the two are independent, so manner won't expose a faker. Grant's test is behavioral asymmetry: how they treat bosses versus receptionists, and whether they say 'I' or 'we' about results.
